beliefs: f strips trailing spaces from the input [E2, E8, E16]

The 'A' exemption holds regardless of length: 'Abc','Abcd','Abcde','Axyz','Axyzw' all unchanged, while 'Hbc','Hbcx','Hbllo','Hello' strip [E10, E13, E14, E16]
Two-character strings like 'Ab','Aa','Hb' are returned unchanged even though first is uppercase and second lowercase [E3, E4, E13, E16]
Strings whose second char is uppercase, digit, space, or symbol are returned unchanged (e.g. 'AB','A1','A1x','A zz','A!zz') [E2, E3, E7, E9]
Contradiction: 'H llo'->' llo' and 'H!llo'->'!llo' strip despite second char being space/symbol, but 'A zz'->'A zz' and 'A!zz'->'A!zz' don't — likely the 'A' exemption again [E6, E9, E11]
Single uppercase letters and strings starting with lowercase/digit/space/empty are returned unchanged after trailing-space strip [E2, E8]
All-uppercase strings starting with 'H' of length >= 3 strip the first character: 'HEL'->'EL','HELL'->'ELL','HELLO'->'ELLO','HELLO!'->'ELLO!' [E14, E15]

Strings starting with 'X' followed by lowercase are NOT stripped ('Xb','Xbc','Xbcd' unchanged), unlike 'H...' — so the strip rule is specific to certain first letters, not all uppercase [E14, E16]
Why does 'HEL' strip but 'ABC' not, and 'Hbc' strip but 'Xbc' not? Possibly the rule keys on specific first letters (H strips, A and X don't) [E14, E15, E16]?
